domain_label: Plated Jewelry Form — Category & Construction Taxonomy and Owner-Scale Producibility
purpose: A method-and-fact engine that classifies fashion/costume jewelry into its full category taxonomy (earrings: studs/hoops/drops; necklaces: chains/pendants/chokers; rings/bands; bracelets/bangles/cuffs; anklets) crossed with construction method (cast, stamped, wire-formed, tube-formed, chain-made, findings-assembled, stone-set) and maps each form to the plating/forming constraints inherited from the supply-side vertical, so an agent can decide [METHOD] which categories are simplest to produce at the owner's small-batch DIY-electroplate/sputter scale without inventing any demand, price, or market-share number.
assumptions: the category and construction taxonomy are well-established domain facts drawn from jewelry manufacture and US FTC Jewelry Guides 16 CFR Part 23 vocabulary; each is tagged [FACT] with basis and never presented as a demand claim

this KB owns FORM (which shapes/categories exist and how they are built and plated), not DEMAND (how many buy / what % / which brands / what price) — those are S1 market KBs and are only pointed at as [METHOD], never answered here

the plating/forming constraints (rack vs barrel plating, Faraday-cage recess starvation, base-metal substrate, wear zones) are inherited as source knowledge from the supply-side vertical (analysis/taxonomy substrate-forming / electro-plating / qc-durability) and the S2 materials specialist; this KB consumes them, it does not re-derive plating chemistry

'owner scale' means small-batch DTC on a headless storefront with DIY electroplating/sputtering, bought-in standard findings and chain, no in-house casting foundry and no automated stone-setting line — the exact equipment envelope is a partial [UNKNOWN] and is carried as a band, not a fixed spec
the producibility ranking of categories is an [ESTIMATE/METHOD] output (a scored decision procedure), explicitly not a measured yield or cost figure; the honest tag travels with it

every non-fact is tagged [ESTIMATE] (with method + confidence) or [UNKNOWN]; no market size, unit count, solid-vs-plated %, demographic rate, competitor brand, or measured price appears anywhere in this KB
exclusions: demand structure, market sizing, solid-vs-plated share, demographics, brand landscape and price tiers (S1 jewel_market KBs) — this KB classifies form, it does not size or price it
shape/motif/silhouette and style-family selection and shape-to-conversion reasoning (this specialist's kb2_shape_motif_style_systems)

sizing/fit standards (ring sizing systems, chain lengths, hoop diameters, post gauges) and the sizing-to-returns link (this specialist's kb3_sizing_fit_returns) — construction is covered here, precise size systems are not

plating chemistry, bath control, thickness-vs-durability curves and the FTC micron thresholds themselves (S2 jewel_materials KBs) — this KB references how form interacts with plating, not how plating is run
the final launch set-of-six selection and the demand-signal synthesis that ranks concrete SKUs (S5 jewel_assortment) — this KB hands off a producible category set, it does not pick the six

competency_questions.question: What is the full US fashion-jewelry category taxonomy by worn-location, and how is it organized as a classification frame?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: TAXONOMY_AXES names the three classifying axes (worn-location category x construction method x plating/forming constraint) and CATEGORY_CONSTRUCTION_MATRIX enumerates earrings/necklaces/rings/bracelets/anklets as the [FACT] top-level worn-location categories with their sub-types cross-referenced to construction methods

competency_questions.question: What are the construction methods a jewelry piece can be built by, including the solid-vs-hollow dimension, and which are ownable at owner scale?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CONSTRUCTION_METHOD_LEXICON lists casting (lost-wax), die-stamping/blanking, wire-forming, tube-forming, machine chain-making, findings assembly, soldering and stone-setting as [FACT], and HOLLOW_VS_SOLID_FORM states the solid (cast/stamped) vs hollow (tube/electroformed/domed) dimension with its weight/cost/plating implications

competency_questions.question: What is the findings and closure taxonomy shared across categories, and why is it the assembly backbone?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: FINDINGS_CLASP_TAXONOMY names ear posts/butterfly & lever backs, jump rings, lobster/spring-ring/toggle clasps, bails and pin stems as [FACT] standard bought-in components and explains that most owner-scale assembly is findings + a formed body, not monolithic casting

competency_questions.question: What is the earrings sub-taxonomy and which earring types are structurally simplest to produce?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: EARRINGS_TAXONOMY enumerates studs, hoops (huggie/endless/click-top), drops/danglers, chandeliers, threaders, ear climbers, jackets and non-pierced ear cuffs with their post/back systems [FACT], and flags flat stamped studs and endless/huggie hoops as the low-component-count structures

competency_questions.question: How are chains, pendants, chokers and anklets constructed, and why are chain-plus-clasp products the simplest assemblies?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: NECKLACE_CHAIN_TAXONOMY names cable/curb/figaro/rope/box/snake/herringbone chain families, pendant/bail construction and choker/lariat forms [FACT], and ANKLET_TAXONOMY states that anklets are a light chain + clasp assembly, the minimal-component chain product

competency_questions.question: What is the rings and bracelets sub-taxonomy and where do casting, forming and stone-setting make a category hard?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: RING_BAND_TAXONOMY names bands/solitaires/signets/stackables/adjustable-open rings and their cast-vs-formed construction, and BRACELET_TAXONOMY names chain/bangle/cuff/tennis/beaded bracelets, flagging tennis (many prong settings + hinge) and rigid cuffs (heavy forming/temper) as the hard structures

competency_questions.question: How does a piece's form map to the plating and forming constraints, and which geometries are hard to plate evenly?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PLATING_FORMING_CONSTRAINT_MAP maps form to rack-vs-barrel plating, substrate and surface area, and PLATING_GEOMETRY_DIFFICULTY explains the Faraday-cage recess-starvation effect, hollow/hinge coverage problems and why flat/convex forms plate more evenly than deep-recessed or moving-joint forms [FACT]

competency_questions.question: How do plating wear zones and skin-contact/nickel exposure differ by category, and why does that shape category choice?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: WEAR_ZONE_DURABILITY_MAP ranks abrasion exposure (rings highest, earrings lowest, bracelets/anklets medium) and SKIN_CONTACT_NICKEL_MAP maps contact duration by category to the EN1811/REACH nickel-release limits (pierced-ear posts the strictest) [FACT]

competency_questions.question: What is the method for scoring a category's producibility at owner scale, and what constraints define 'owner scale'?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ASSEMBLY_COMPLEXITY_INDEX defines a [METHOD] score over component count, solder joints, plating passes, setting operations and moving parts, and OWNER_SCALE_CONSTRAINTS states the small-batch DIY-plating / bought-findings / no-casting-foundry envelope as the scoring context

competency_questions.question: Which categories are simplest to produce at owner scale, and how is a candidate form screened in or out?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SIMPLEST_TO_PRODUCE_RANKING gives the [METHOD/ESTIMATE] ordering (stamped studs, pendant-on-bought-chain, endless/huggie hoops, anklets/chain bracelets simplest; cast/stone-set rings, tennis bracelets, rigid cuffs hardest) and FORM_PRODUCIBILITY_SCREEN gives the pass/fail screen (owner-producible? plating-friendly geometry? acceptable wear/skin zone?)

competency_questions.question: How does standard-findings modularity reduce production complexity across the category set?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: STANDARDIZATION_MODULARITY explains that sharing bought posts/chains/clasps/bails across SKUs collapses the assembly-complexity and plating-batch burden, and names the SKU-variety cost of over-standardizing

competency_questions.question: What does the form work hand off, and how is the FACT taxonomy kept separate from the METHOD producibility judgment and the demand questions it must not answer?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: TAXONOMY_HONESTY_LEDGER separates the [FACT] taxonomy/construction/FTC anchors from the [METHOD/ESTIMATE] producibility ranking and the [UNKNOWN] owner equipment envelope, and FORM_HANDOFF delivers the producible category set with construction+constraint tags to kb2/kb3/S2/S5, stopping before demand ranking and style selection

glossary.definition: The top-level [FACT] taxonomy axis grouping fashion jewelry by where it is worn: earrings, necklaces/neckwear, rings, bracelets, and anklets; each splits into sub-types (e.g. earrings -> studs/hoops/drops) and is the frame the owner's 'which type' question is organized against, kept strictly separate from any demand claim about the category.

The [FACT] fabrication route by which a piece is built: lost-wax casting, die-striking/stamping/blanking, wire-forming/wrapping, tube-forming, machine chain-making, findings assembly, soldering/laser-welding, and stone-setting (prong/bezel/pave/channel); a category is producible at owner scale only if its dominant method is ownable without a casting foundry or automated setting line.

The standard, typically bought-in functional components that join or close a piece [FACT]: ear posts and butterfly/lever/screw backs, jump rings, lobster/spring-ring/toggle clasps, bails, head/eye pins, ear wires and pin stems; owner-scale production is mostly a formed body plus catalog findings, not a monolithic casting.

The US Federal Trade Commission Jewelry Guides definitions this KB uses for finish terms only as vocabulary [FACT]: 'gold electroplate' (>=0.175 micron fine gold), 'vermeil' (>=2.5 micron of >=10k gold over sterling silver), 'gold-filled/rolled gold plate' (mechanically bonded gold layer by weight fraction), 'sterling silver' (92.5% Ag); the micron thresholds themselves are owned by the S2 materials KB, not decided here.

Rhodium is a hard, bright-white, tarnish-resistant platinum-group metal commonly electroplated over sterling silver or white gold to give a bright white finish and slow the silver's tarnish [FACT]; in this KB it matters only as a form-relevant fact (thin rhodium wears at high-abrasion zones), the plating science is S2's.

The two owner-scale electroplating modes [FACT]: rack plating hangs individual pieces on a wired rack for controlled, even coverage of larger/statement forms; barrel (bulk) plating tumbles many small parts together, cheap and fast for chains, jump rings and small findings but poor for recesses and delicate forms; a form's size and geometry decide which mode fits.

The electroplating fact that current density is lowest inside recesses, deep channels, hollows and behind protrusions, so plating there is thinner or absent (the Faraday-cage effect) [FACT]; deeply recessed, filigree, hollow or hinged forms plate unevenly, while flat and convex forms plate uniformly — a core form-to-plating constraint.

The region of a worn piece exposed to abrasion/friction that thins plating fastest [FACT-durability]: ring shanks and signet faces (highest, hand contact), bracelet/anklet undersides and clasps (medium), earring bodies (lowest, little contact); category choice trades on how visible plating wear will be, informing thickness needs handed to S2.

A scored decision procedure (not a measured cost) that rates a candidate form's owner-scale producibility by counting components, solder/weld joints, plating passes, stone-setting operations and moving parts; higher score = harder to make at small batch; used to rank categories and screen candidates, always carried as [METHOD/ESTIMATE] with its confidence, never as a yield or cost fact.

The production envelope assumed throughout: small-batch DTC on a headless storefront, DIY electroplating/sputtering, bought-in standard findings and chain, hand assembly, and NO in-house casting foundry or automated stone-setting line; the exact equipment limits are a partial [UNKNOWN] carried as a band, and the producibility ranking is only valid inside this envelope.

source_registry.citation_or_locator: heuristic prior; no external dataset supplied

nodes.definition: Establish the classification frame the whole KB hangs on: fashion/costume jewelry form is organized on three orthogonal [FACT] axes — (1) worn-location category (earrings, necklaces/neckwear, rings, bracelets, anklets), (2) construction method (cast, stamped, wire-formed, tube-formed, chain-made, findings-assembled, stone-set), and (3) plating/forming constraint (plating mode, geometry, substrate, wear zone). The owner's 'which type / which shape' question is answered on axis 1 x 2, and 'which is simplest to produce' is answered by folding axis 3 onto that grid. This frame is deliberately demand-free: it names what exists and how it is built, never how many sell — that is the S1 market specialist's job.

included: the three classifying axes and their role
category x construction as the answer grid for 'which type/shape'
the demand-free boundary of the frame

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a category-axis or frame change occurs

pros.claim: A three-axis frame lets every later node attach to a fixed coordinate instead of a loose list, keeping the taxonomy and the producibility judgment cleanly separated
pros.example: a 'huggie hoop' is category=earring/hoop x method=tube-or-wire x constraint=small-barrel-platable, a full coordinate

cons.claim: Real pieces can blend categories and methods, so the axes are a simplifying grid not a partition
cons.example: an ear-cuff-plus-chain 'ear jacket' spans earring and chain construction

failure_modes: collapsing construction into category so producibility can no longer be read off
letting a demand assumption leak into what is meant to be a pure form frame
acceptance_tests: the three axes (worn-location category, construction method, plating/forming constraint) are named and the category x construction grid is stated as the frame for the owner's 'which type/shape' question, with the demand-free boundary explicit
revisit_triggers: a new worn-location category enters the assortment scope (e.g. body/nose jewelry)
the S1 market frame renames the category axis
a hybrid form recurs often enough to need its own coordinate

nodes.definition: Enumerate the construction-method axis as a precise [FACT] lexicon: lost-wax casting (molten metal into a mould, rich 3D forms, needs a casting setup); die-striking / stamping / blanking (sheet metal pressed or punched, ideal for flat charms, studs, tags); wire-forming and wire-wrapping (bending round/half-round wire into hoops, jump rings, ear wires); tube-forming (seamless/seamed tube for hollow hoops and light bodies); machine chain-making vs hand-linked-and-soldered chain; findings assembly (joining a body to bought posts/clasps/bails with jump rings and solder); soldering / laser-welding; and stone-setting (prong, bezel, pave, channel). Each category later inherits its dominant method, and owner-scale producibility is largely 'is the dominant method ownable without a foundry or an automated setting line'.

included: the full construction-method lexicon as [FACT]
which methods need heavy capital (casting, automated setting) vs hand tools (wire, stamping, assembly)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a construction-method capability or classification changes

pros.claim: A shared method lexicon means every category node can name its build route in the same vocabulary, making producibility comparable across categories
pros.example: studs='stamping', hoops='wire/tube', anklets='chain+assembly' all read on one scale

cons.claim: A method list flattens skill and tooling differences within a method (hand vs CNC stamping) that matter at the margin
cons.example: hand-sawn blanks and die-struck blanks are both 'stamping' but differ hugely in throughput

failure_modes: treating casting as a default when owner scale has no foundry
omitting findings-assembly as a method and undercounting bought-in components
acceptance_tests: casting, stamping/blanking, wire-forming, tube-forming, chain-making, findings assembly, soldering and stone-setting are each named as [FACT] with which are capital-heavy vs hand-ownable
revisit_triggers: the owner acquires or loses a method capability (e.g. gets a casting/3D-resin setup)
a new fabrication route becomes owner-affordable
a category's dominant method is reclassified

nodes.definition: Enumerate the shared findings/closure taxonomy that is the assembly backbone of almost every category [FACT]: ear posts with friction/butterfly push-backs, screw-backs, la-pousette locking backs, lever-backs, French/fish-hook wires and clip-ons (earrings); jump rings and split rings (universal joiners); lobster-claw, spring-ring, toggle, box and magnetic clasps (chains/bracelets/anklets); bails and pinch-bails (pendants); head pins, eye pins and pin stems (drops and brooches). The key owner-scale fact: most pieces are a formed or stamped body plus catalog findings joined by jump rings and a little solder, so the findings taxonomy — not casting — is where owner-scale assembly lives, and standardizing on a few finding types is a direct complexity lever.

included: ear backs, jump rings, clasps, bails and pins as [FACT] bought-in components
the body+findings assembly model as the owner-scale norm
excluded: which finding a given SKU uses (assortment)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a findings standard or finish-match issue changes

pros.claim: Cataloguing findings as shared bought-in parts shows most categories converge on the same small component set, which is what makes standardization and small-batch assembly feasible
pros.example: the same lobster clasp + jump rings close a necklace, a bracelet and an anklet

cons.claim: Bought-in findings must themselves be plated/quality-matched, adding a coordination burden the taxonomy alone does not solve
cons.example: a raw-brass clasp on a rhodium body creates a colour/tarnish mismatch unless co-plated or pre-finished

failure_modes: ignoring lever-back/hinge findings' moving-part complexity
mismatching finding finish/metal to the body finish
acceptance_tests: ear backs, jump rings, lobster/spring-ring/toggle clasps, bails and pins are named as [FACT] bought-in findings and the body+findings assembly model is stated as the owner-scale norm
revisit_triggers: a finding type is standardized or dropped across the line
a findings supplier or finish-match issue arises
a hinge/lever finding's reliability becomes a returns driver

nodes.definition: Bridge form to the supply-side plating/forming constraints inherited from the vertical: a piece's size and geometry decide its plating mode (small parts and chains -> barrel/bulk plating; larger statement/rack-worthy forms -> rack plating), its substrate (brass, sterling 925, stainless, etc. from S2) sets adhesion and colour, its surface area drives plating time and precious-metal consumption, and its wear zone sets the thickness needed to survive. This node is the interface: it does not run the plating bath, it states which form attributes map to which inherited constraint so downstream producibility can score them. All thresholds (microns, bath specifics) are owned by S2 and only referenced here.

included: form-attribute -> plating-mode / substrate / surface-area / wear-zone mapping
the interface role to the supply-side and S2

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a plating mode, substrate or wear-zone constraint changes

pros.claim: An explicit form-to-constraint bridge stops the taxonomy from being decorative — every category's shape now carries its plating consequence
pros.example: a fine chain maps to barrel plating + high tangling surface area, a signet ring maps to rack plating + high wear zone

cons.claim: The mapping is qualitative until S2 supplies real bath/thickness numbers, so it guides selection but cannot yet quantify plating cost
cons.example: 'high surface area' flags gold consumption but the dollar figure waits on S2/S6

failure_modes: choosing a form whose plating mode the owner cannot run (rack-only statement piece with barrel-only kit)
ignoring substrate-to-form adhesion mismatch inherited from S2
acceptance_tests: the mapping from form size/geometry to plating mode (barrel vs rack), substrate, surface area and wear zone is stated, with micron/bath thresholds explicitly deferred to S2
revisit_triggers: S2 updates a substrate or thickness constraint
the owner's plating kit changes (adds rack capacity or larger barrel)
a form is found un-platable in the owner's available mode

nodes.definition: Establish the solid-vs-hollow construction dimension that cuts across categories [FACT]: solid forms (cast or thick-stamped) are heavy, use more metal, are dent-resistant and plate predictably on their outer surface; hollow forms (seamed/seamless tube, electroformed shells, domed-and-joined stampings, puffed hoops) use far less metal (lower cost and lower precious-plating consumption per size) and feel lighter, but are dent- and crush-prone, can trap plating solution or gas in cavities, and plate poorly on interior surfaces (Faraday starvation). Hollow tube hoops and lightweight puffed pendants are a classic owner-scale cost lever; solid stamped studs are the simplest robust form. The choice trades metal cost and weight against durability and plating evenness.

included: solid vs hollow as a cross-category construction dimension
the weight/metal-cost vs durability/plating-evenness tradeoff

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a hollow-form durability or metal-cost signal changes

pros.claim: Naming hollow-vs-solid as its own dimension exposes a real cost lever (hollow = less metal) alongside its durability cost, before any category is chosen
pros.example: a hollow tube hoop can weigh a fraction of a solid one, cutting metal and plating cost per piece

cons.claim: Hollow forms introduce trapped-solution and crush-failure modes that a naive cost-only read would miss
cons.example: plating solution left in a hollow hoop bleeds out later and stains or corrodes the piece

failure_modes: choosing hollow purely for cost and shipping dent-prone pieces that drive returns
assuming a hollow form's interior is plated when it is Faraday-starved
acceptance_tests: the solid (cast/stamped, heavy, robust) vs hollow (tube/electroformed/domed, light, cheap, dent- and starvation-prone) dimension is stated with its cost-vs-durability tradeoff
revisit_triggers: a hollow-form return/dent rate signal appears
metal price moves enough to change the hollow cost incentive
a trapped-solution QC failure recurs

nodes.definition: Enumerate the earrings category [FACT]: studs (flat/prong/bezel face on a straight post), hoops (endless/self-closing, click-top/hinged, and huggies), drops/danglers (a body hung off a post or wire), chandeliers (multi-tier drops), threaders (chain through the lobe), ear climbers/crawlers, ear jackets, and non-pierced ear cuffs and clip-ons. Back/closure systems: friction butterfly, screw, la-pousette, lever-back, French/fish-hook. Construction reads off the method lexicon: studs = stamped/cast face + soldered post; endless and huggie hoops = wire/tube-formed; drops = body + findings assembly. Structurally, a flat stamped stud (two parts: face + post) and an endless/huggie hoop (one formed wire) are the lowest-component-count earring forms; chandeliers and lever-back drops are the highest.

included: the full earring sub-taxonomy and back systems as [FACT]
per-type dominant construction and component count
excluded: post gauge / hoop diameter sizing standards (kb3)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: an earring sub-type or back-system fact changes

pros.claim: Breaking earrings into sub-types with component counts makes the 'simplest earring' answer fall out structurally rather than by taste
pros.example: a stud is 2 parts + 1 solder while a chandelier is a dozen findings + multiple joins

cons.claim: Pierced-ear posts carry the strictest skin-contact nickel limit, so 'simplest to make' is not automatically 'simplest to sell safely'
cons.example: a cheap-alloy stud post can breach the pierced-ear nickel limit even though it is easy to stamp

failure_modes: treating all hoops as equal when click-top/hinged hoops add a moving joint
ignoring the post's skin-contact constraint when calling studs simplest
acceptance_tests: studs, hoops (endless/huggie/click-top), drops, chandeliers, threaders, climbers, jackets and non-pierced cuffs are named with their back systems and per-type construction, and stamped studs + endless/huggie hoops are flagged as lowest-component-count
revisit_triggers: a new earring sub-type enters scope
a back-system reliability or skin-contact issue arises
kb3 revises post/hoop size standards affecting construction

nodes.definition: Enumerate the neckwear category [FACT]: chain families by link geometry — cable, curb/Cuban, figaro, rope, box/Venetian, snake, herringbone, Singapore, wheat/spiga, and ball/bead chain — each with distinct flexibility, kink-resistance and plating behaviour (flat herringbone and snake plate broad even surfaces but kink; open cable/curb links barrel-plate well); pendants (a stamped/cast/wire body hung from a bail on a chain); chokers (short close-fitting chains or bands); lariats/Y-necklaces and station necklaces. Construction: chain is normally bought or machine-made by the metre and cut-to-length, then finished with bought clasps and jump rings — so a pendant-on-a-bought-chain is one of the lowest-effort finished products at owner scale (form the pendant, buy the chain and clasp, assemble). Hand-linked soldered chain is the high-effort exception.

included: chain families, pendant/bail, choker/lariat/station forms as [FACT]
bought-chain + clasp + pendant as the low-effort finished-product path

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a chain-family or pendant-construction fact changes

pros.claim: Distinguishing bought machine chain from hand-linked chain shows why pendant-on-chain is near the floor of production effort at owner scale
pros.example: a stamped pendant + a spool of bought cable chain + lobster clasps yields a finished SKU with one forming step

cons.claim: Some chain styles (herringbone, snake) kink permanently and plate/wear in ways that raise returns despite easy assembly
cons.example: a plated herringbone that kinks shows a bright wear line at the crease

failure_modes: assuming all chain is equally durable when herringbone/snake kink-fail
hand-linking chain that could be bought, inflating effort needlessly
acceptance_tests: cable/curb/figaro/rope/box/snake/herringbone chain families, pendant/bail construction and choker/lariat/station forms are named [FACT], with pendant-on-bought-chain flagged as a low-effort finished path
revisit_triggers: a chain-style durability (kink) signal appears
a bought-chain supply or finish-match issue arises
kb3 revises necklace length standards

nodes.definition: Enumerate the rings category [FACT]: plain bands (flat, D-shape, comfort-fit), solitaires and halos (a set stone on a shank), signets (a flat engravable face), stackables (thin narrow bands worn in groups), eternity/half-eternity (stones around the shank), cocktail/statement rings, and adjustable/open rings (an incomplete shank sized by bending). Construction is the category's difficulty story: fine-detailed and stone-set rings are dominantly cast-and-set (needs a casting setup + setting skill), while plain bands and open/adjustable bands can be formed from stamped strip or wire and soldered/left open. Rings also sit in the highest plating wear zone (constant hand contact) and are the category where owner-scale casting/setting limits bite hardest — an adjustable open band is producible, a pave-set cast cocktail ring largely is not.

included: ring sub-types and their cast-vs-formed construction as [FACT]
the casting/setting dependence that makes most rings hard at owner scale

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a ring construction capability or wear signal changes

pros.claim: Splitting rings by construction shows the category is bimodal: adjustable/plain formed bands are owner-doable while cast stone-set rings largely are not
pros.example: an open adjustable band is bent from plated strip; a halo solitaire needs casting + prong-setting

cons.claim: Rings' highest-wear-zone position means even producible bands need extra plating thickness to survive, raising their real cost
cons.example: a thin gold flash on a ring shank wears through at the finger-back within weeks

failure_modes: planning cast stone-set rings the owner cannot make or set
shipping a ring with a thin plating that fails fast in the high-wear zone
acceptance_tests: bands, solitaires, signets, stackables, eternity, cocktail and adjustable/open rings are named with cast-vs-formed construction, and the casting/setting dependence plus highest-wear-zone position are stated
revisit_triggers: the owner gains casting/setting capability
a ring plating-wear complaint signal appears
kb3 changes ring sizing affecting formed-band construction

nodes.definition: Enumerate the wrist category [FACT]: chain/link bracelets (a short necklace-style chain + clasp), bangles (rigid closed rings slipped over the hand), cuffs (rigid open C-shape sprung onto the wrist), tennis bracelets (a flexible line of individually prong-set stones + a hinge/box clasp), beaded/elastic and charm bracelets. Construction spread is wide: a chain/link bracelet is bought-chain-plus-clasp assembly (near the production floor, like an anklet); a bangle is a formed and joined loop needing size/temper control; a rigid cuff needs heavy forming and spring temper to hold shape; a tennis bracelet is the hardest common form (dozens of settings + a reliable hinge clasp). Wear zone is medium (undersides and clasp abrade). The category thus contains both one of the easiest (chain bracelet) and one of the hardest (tennis) owner-scale products.

included: chain/bangle/cuff/tennis/beaded bracelet sub-types and construction as [FACT]
the easy(chain) vs hard(tennis/cuff) spread within one category

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a bracelet construction capability or fit signal changes

pros.claim: Showing the category spans easiest-to-hardest prevents a blanket 'bracelets are easy/hard' error and points production at chain bracelets
pros.example: a chain bracelet is anklet-like assembly while a tennis bracelet needs many settings + a hinge

cons.claim: Rigid bangles/cuffs need forming and temper the owner may lack, so the easy label only covers the chain sub-type
cons.example: a cuff that lacks spring temper splays and will not stay on the wrist

failure_modes: planning tennis or rigid cuffs beyond owner forming/setting capability
treating a bangle's size/temper control as trivial
acceptance_tests: chain/link, bangle, cuff, tennis and beaded bracelets are named with construction, and the easy(chain-bracelet) vs hard(tennis/cuff) spread is stated
revisit_triggers: the owner gains forming/temper or setting capability
a bangle/cuff fit or spring-failure signal appears
kb3 revises wrist sizing

nodes.definition: Enumerate the anklet category [FACT]: it is dominantly a light chain (cable, curb, figaro, satellite/station, ball) cut to ankle length and closed with a lobster or spring-ring clasp, often with an extender chain for adjustability and sometimes small charms or stations. Construction is the minimal case of the neckwear path: bought chain + bought clasp + optional bought charms + jump-ring assembly, with no forming, casting or setting needed. Wear zone is medium (ground/shoe abrasion on the underside) and skin contact is intermittent. Because it inherits the chain families wholesale and adds essentially no new forming operation, the anklet is the structurally simplest finished category in the whole taxonomy — the reference floor against which other categories' effort is measured.

nodes.definition: Detail the geometry-driven plating-difficulty gradient [FACT]: electroplating deposits unevenly as a function of shape because current density concentrates on edges/points and is starved in recesses, deep channels, hollows and behind protrusions (the Faraday-cage effect). Consequently flat and gently convex forms (stamped studs, flat pendants, plain bands, open cable/curb links) plate uniformly and reliably; deeply recessed, filigree, textured, hollow-interior and hinged/moving-joint forms (chandeliers, textured signets, tennis settings, click-top hinges, herringbone crevices) plate unevenly, need auxiliary anodes or robbers, and show early wear or discoloration at starved spots. This gradient is a first-class producibility input: geometry difficulty is largely why some categories are hard to plate well at owner scale, independent of assembly effort.

included: the flat/convex-easy vs recessed/hollow/hinged-hard plating gradient and its Faraday-cage basis [FACT]
geometry difficulty as a standalone producibility input

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a plating-geometry capability or failure signal changes

pros.claim: Separating plating-geometry difficulty from assembly effort captures a form that is easy to assemble but hard to plate evenly
pros.example: a textured filigree pendant is quick to hang on a chain but starves plating in its recesses

cons.claim: Auxiliary anodes/robbers can partly rescue hard geometries, so the gradient is a tendency not an absolute bar
cons.example: a shaped anode improves recess coverage on a signet, at added setup cost

failure_modes: choosing a deeply-recessed statement form the owner's simple bath cannot cover evenly
ignoring hinge/interior starvation and shipping pieces that wear early at hidden spots
acceptance_tests: the Faraday-cage recess-starvation effect is stated and forms are graded flat/convex-easy vs recessed/hollow/hinged-hard, with geometry difficulty named as a producibility input distinct from assembly effort
revisit_triggers: the owner adds auxiliary-anode/robber capability
a starvation/wear QC failure recurs on a geometry class

nodes.definition: Map plating wear/abrasion exposure by category [FACT-durability], because a plated finish's perceived quality is set by how visibly it wears: rings sit in the highest-abrasion zone (constant hand/surface contact on shank and face), so plating thins and shows base metal fastest; bracelets, bangles, cuffs and anklets are medium (undersides, clasps and — for anklets — shoe/ground contact abrade); necklace chains are low-to-medium (clasp and neck contact); earrings are lowest (little rubbing). This map does not set micron thickness (S2 owns that) but tells the form specialist which categories demand thicker/harder finishes (or rhodium/hard-gold) to survive and which tolerate thin flash — a direct input to which categories are safe to launch at owner plating capability.

included: the category abrasion-exposure ranking (rings high, earrings low) as [FACT-durability]

excluded: the micron thickness spec and durability test protocol (S2)

pros.claim: Ranking wear zones tells the owner which categories will look worn fastest, guiding away from thin-plated high-wear forms at launch
pros.example: a thin-gold ring shows wear far sooner than the same plating on a stud

cons.claim: Wear also depends on the wearer and thickness (S2), so the ranking is a relative-exposure guide not an absolute lifetime
cons.example: a thick hard-gold ring can outlast a thin-flash earring despite the higher wear zone

failure_modes: launching a thin-plated ring line whose wear drives complaints
treating the exposure ranking as an absolute durability number rather than a relative guide

nodes.definition: Map skin-contact exposure by category and tie it to the nickel-release rule [FACT]: pierced-ear posts and studs are inserted into a wound/piercing and worn continuously, the strictest case; rings and bracelets/bangles/cuffs are prolonged direct contact; necklaces and anklets are prolonged but lighter/intermittent contact. Under EU REACH Annex XVII (the EN1811 test method), post assemblies inserted into pierced ears must release <0.2 ug/cm2/week and other prolonged-skin-contact items <0.5 ug/cm2/week; the US has no identical federal limit but the same nickel-allergy science applies and hypoallergenic positioning matters to the 18-25 skin-contact wearer. This makes the earring-post substrate a safety-gated form decision (favouring nickel-safe bases / barrier plating), not merely a cost choice — the one place 'simplest to stamp' collides with 'safe to sell'.

included: skin-contact-duration ranking by category and the pierced-ear vs prolonged nickel-release limits as [FACT]
the earring-post substrate as a safety-gated form decision
excluded: the substrate/barrier plating spec and nickel spot-test protocol (S2)
US market demographic allergy rates (S1, and unmeasured -> [UNKNOWN])

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a nickel-limit, reaction signal or substrate recommendation changes

pros.claim: Tying contact duration to the nickel limits makes skin-safety an explicit form gate, especially for earring posts, before a cheap alloy is chosen
pros.example: flagging the pierced-ear <0.2 ug/cm2/week limit steers stud posts to nickel-safe bases

cons.claim: The EU limit is a regulatory anchor, not a US mandate, so it is used as a safety benchmark and its US legal force is [UNKNOWN] to this KB
cons.example: a US-only seller is not automatically bound by REACH but the allergy risk is real

failure_modes: choosing a cheap high-nickel post substrate that breaches the pierced-ear benchmark
overstating the EU limit as a US legal requirement
acceptance_tests: skin-contact duration is ranked by category and the pierced-ear <0.2 and prolonged <0.5 ug/cm2/week nickel-release limits (EN1811/REACH) are stated as [FACT], with earring posts flagged as the safety-gated form decision and US legal force marked [UNKNOWN]

nodes.definition: Define the production envelope every producibility judgment is relative to [FACT on the model / partial UNKNOWN on exact limits]: small-batch DTC on a headless storefront; DIY electroplating and sputtering (limited bath size, likely barrel + modest rack capacity); bought-in standard findings and chain; hand assembly with jump rings, solder/torch and simple forming (pliers, mandrels, a stamping/press capability); and critically NO in-house casting foundry and NO automated stone-setting line. Capital, batch size, plating-bath dimensions and rack throughput are the binding limits, and their exact values are a partial [UNKNOWN] carried as a band. This envelope is what makes 'simplest to produce' meaningful: a category is simple only if its dominant method and plating mode fit inside this envelope; the ranking is invalid if quoted outside it.

included: the small-batch DIY-plating / bought-findings / no-casting-foundry envelope as the scoring context
the exact equipment limits as a partial [UNKNOWN] band

pros.example: 'studs are simplest' is stated as true within DIY-plate/no-foundry scale, not universally

cons.example: a larger acquired plating tank could move rack-only statement forms into reach

failure_modes: quoting the producibility ranking as if it held at contract-manufacturing scale
hardening the [UNKNOWN] equipment limits into false precision

nodes.definition: Define the [METHOD] producibility score that turns the category matrix into a rankable number: for a candidate form, count and weight (a) distinct components (body + findings), (b) forming operations (stamp/bend/tube), (c) solder/weld joints, (d) plating passes and plating-mode fit (barrel-ok vs rack-required vs geometry-starved), (e) stone-setting operations, and (f) moving parts (hinges, lever-backs, spring temper). Higher weighted sum = harder at owner scale. It is explicitly a decision-procedure score, not a measured cost or yield: it is carried as [METHOD/ESTIMATE] with a confidence, and its weights are tunable and to be recalibrated against real build outcomes. It reads the CATEGORY_CONSTRUCTION_MATRIX and PLATING_GEOMETRY_DIFFICULTY as inputs and feeds the ranking and the screen.

included: the weighted producibility scoring dimensions as a [METHOD]

excluded: the owner-scale envelope it is scored within (OWNER_SCALE_CONSTRAINTS)

cons.claim: Index weights are priors until calibrated on real builds, so the score orders categories more reliably than it sizes the gap
cons.example: the stud-vs-hoop gap may be smaller in practice than the default weights imply

failure_modes: reporting the index as a measured cost/yield rather than a [METHOD] score
leaving weights uncalibrated and over-trusting the absolute values
acceptance_tests: the index is defined over components, forming ops, solder joints, plating passes/mode-fit, setting ops and moving parts as a weighted [METHOD] score, tagged as a tunable decision-procedure not a measured cost/yield

nodes.definition: Produce the headline [METHOD/ESTIMATE] answer to the owner's 'which categories are simplest to produce at my scale': applying the complexity index within the owner envelope, the simplest tier is flat stamped studs, pendant-on-bought-chain necklaces, endless/huggie hoops (wire/tube), anklets and chain bracelets (bought-chain + clasp assembly); the middle tier is drop earrings, station/charm chains, plain/adjustable formed rings and bangles; the hardest tier is cast-and-stone-set rings (solitaires/halos/pave), tennis bracelets (many settings + hinge) and rigid spring-temper cuffs, plus any deeply-recessed or hinged statement form. nodes.definition: State the modularity lever [METHOD]: sharing a small set of standard bought-in components (one or two post styles, a common chain gauge, one lobster clasp family, a standard bail) across many SKUs collapses the assembly-complexity and plating-batch burden — the same findings are ordered in volume, plated in the same barrel run, and assembled with the same jig, so incremental SKUs mostly vary the formed body, not the whole build. This is the same value-engineering logic S2 applies to materials, expressed for form. Its cost is variety: over-standardizing can make the range look samey and constrains distinct style expression (a kb2/assortment tension). The lever is to standardize the invisible functional findings and vary the visible body.

nodes.definition: Define the pass/fail screen that admits or rejects a candidate form for owner-scale launch consideration [METHOD]: (1) is its dominant construction method ownable in the envelope (no foundry/automated-setting dependence)? (2) is its geometry plating-friendly in the owner's available mode (flat/convex + barrel/rack-fit, not deeply-recessed/hinged-starved)? (3) does its wear zone tolerate the owner's achievable plating thickness/hardness, or is it a thin-flash-on-high-wear reject? (4) if it is skin-contact-critical (earring post), does the substrate meet the nickel benchmark? A form must pass all four to enter the assortment candidate set; failing any is a reject or a redesign trigger (e.g. make a recessed pendant shallower, swap a cast ring for a formed band). This screen is the operational gate the ranking feeds into.

reject-or-redesign as the outcome of a failed test

conflict_axes.name: taxonomy_breadth_vs_owner_producibility
conflict_axes.description: The full [FACT] category taxonomy is broad while only a subset is producible at owner scale; presenting all categories as equally launchable misleads.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: keep the full taxonomy as reference and let the producibility ranking + screen decide the launch candidate set

conflict_axes.name: cast_richness_vs_fabricated_ownability
conflict_axes.description: Casting yields rich 3D and stone-set forms but needs a foundry/setting line, while stamped/wire/tube fabrication is owner-ownable but formally limited.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: restrict to fabricated forms in the current envelope; treat cast/stone-set as out-of-envelope unless capability is added or outsourced

conflict_axes.name: hollow_cost_saving_vs_durability
conflict_axes.description: Hollow construction saves metal and plating cost and weight but is dent-prone and Faraday-starved inside, hurting durability.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: use hollow only in low-wear categories and keep solid where wear zone is medium/high

conflict_axes.name: barrel_bulk_vs_rack_control
conflict_axes.description: Barrel plating is cheap/fast for small parts and chains but starves recesses and damages delicate forms, while rack plating is controlled but slow and capacity-limited.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: barrel-plate small robust parts (chains, jump rings, studs) and rack-plate larger/delicate/recessed forms, choosing forms that fit the owner's available mode

conflict_axes.name: buy_findings_vs_make_findings
conflict_axes.description: Bought standard findings are cheap, consistent and modular but constrain form, while making findings in-house frees design at the cost of effort and consistency.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: default to bought standard findings for owner-scale consistency and modularity; make findings only where a signature form demands it

conflict_axes.name: high_wear_appeal_vs_plating_longevity
conflict_axes.description: Rings and high-contact forms are appealing but sit in the highest wear zone where thin owner-achievable plating fails visibly fastest.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: only launch high-wear forms if the owner can achieve adequate thickness/hardness (or rhodium/hard-gold via S2); else prefer low-wear categories

conflict_axes.name: cheap_substrate_vs_skin_safety
conflict_axes.description: The cheapest base metals may exceed the pierced-ear nickel-release limit, colliding with the safety needs of continuous skin/piercing contact.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: for skin-contact-critical forms, especially earring posts, let the nickel benchmark override the cheapest substrate via nickel-safe base or barrier plating

conflict_axes.name: moving_part_complexity_vs_reliability
conflict_axes.description: Hinges, lever-backs, click-tops and tennis clasps add desirable function but are moving-part failure points and raise assembly complexity.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: prefer static closures (endless hoops, friction backs, lobster clasps) at owner scale; add hinges/levers only when reliability is proven

conflict_axes.name: fact_taxonomy_vs_method_ranking
conflict_axes.description: The taxonomy and construction facts are firm while the producibility ranking is a tunable envelope-conditional estimate; conflating them overstates the ranking's certainty.
poles: keep the ranking a labelled estimate
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: carry the taxonomy as [FACT] and the ranking as [METHOD/ESTIMATE] conditional on the owner envelope, never hardening the ranking into a fact

conflict_axes.name: producibility_vs_demand_boundary
conflict_axes.description: This KB can say a form is easy to make but must not say it will sell; simplest-to-produce is tempting to read as best-to-launch.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: treat a producibility pass as necessary-not-sufficient and hand off to S5 to combine with S1 demand and kb2 style before any launch pick

edge_cases.description: A form is trivial to assemble but Faraday-starved to plate, so it looks easy on the complexity count yet fails plating coverage
edge_cases.trigger: a deeply-recessed, filigree or hollow-interior body is scored on assembly alone
edge_cases.mitigation: score plating-geometry difficulty as its own index dimension and reject or shallow-redesign starved forms in the screen

edge_cases.description: A cheap high-nickel stud post breaches the pierced-ear nickel-release benchmark even though the stud is the simplest form to stamp
edge_cases.trigger: the cheapest substrate is chosen for an earring post on producibility grounds alone
edge_cases.mitigation: gate earring posts on the nickel benchmark, using a nickel-safe base or barrier plating regardless of the form's low assembly cost

edge_cases.description: The simplest-to-produce ranking is read as a demand or best-to-launch ranking and the assortment is built on ease of making alone
edge_cases.trigger: a launch decision leads on producibility without S1 demand or kb2 style
edge_cases.mitigation: treat producibility as necessary-not-sufficient and hand off to S5 to combine with demand and style

edge_cases.description: A cast stone-set ring is planned inside an envelope with no foundry or setting line
edge_cases.trigger: a ring sub-type requiring casting/setting is admitted without checking the owner envelope
edge_cases.mitigation: reject cast/stone-set rings in-envelope or redesign to a formed/adjustable band; add the capability or outsource before revisiting

edge_cases.description: A thin plating on a high-wear ring or bracelet clasp wears through to base metal within weeks and drives complaints
edge_cases.trigger: a high-wear-zone form is launched at a plating thickness the owner can achieve but that is too thin for the zone
edge_cases.mitigation: require adequate thickness/hardness (or rhodium/hard-gold via S2) for high-wear forms, else prefer low-wear categories

edge_cases.description: Plating solution or gas is trapped inside a hollow hoop and later bleeds out, staining or corroding the piece
edge_cases.trigger: a sealed hollow form is barrel-plated without a drain/vent path
edge_cases.mitigation: design vent/drain holes into hollow forms or avoid sealed hollows in the plating line

edge_cases.description: A herringbone or snake chain kinks permanently and shows a bright wear line at the crease despite being an easy bought-chain assembly
edge_cases.trigger: a kink-prone flat chain style is chosen purely for easy assembly
edge_cases.mitigation: prefer kink-resistant link styles (cable, curb, rope) for durable everyday pieces, reserving herringbone/snake for lower-stress uses

edge_cases.description: A bought clasp or post in raw brass is assembled onto a rhodium/gold body, creating a colour and tarnish mismatch
edge_cases.trigger: findings are not finish-matched or co-plated with the body
edge_cases.mitigation: co-plate findings with the body or buy pre-finished findings in the matching finish

edge_cases.description: The producibility ranking is quoted at contract-manufacturing scale where casting and setting are cheap, inverting the owner-scale order
edge_cases.trigger: the ranking is used outside the owner envelope it is conditioned on
edge_cases.mitigation: always state the ranking as conditional on the owner envelope and re-run it if the envelope changes

edge_cases.description: Standardization is pushed onto visible elements so every SKU looks the same and the range reads as one product
edge_cases.trigger: shared components extend from invisible findings to the visible body
edge_cases.mitigation: standardize invisible functional findings only and vary the visible body, deferring the variety limit to kb2/S5

edge_cases.description: A demand/price/share/demographic/brand answer is written into the form KB because the owner asked for it
edge_cases.trigger: a market question is answered here instead of being routed to S1
edge_cases.mitigation: route every demand/price/share/demographic/brand question to S1 as [METHOD]/[UNKNOWN]; the form KB answers only form

workflow.description: State worn-location category x construction method x plating/forming constraint as the demand-free frame the KB hangs on
workflow.gate: the three axes and the category x construction answer grid are stated with the demand-free boundary

workflow.action: Enumerate construction methods and the solid/hollow dimension
workflow.description: List casting/stamping/wire/tube/chain/assembly/soldering/setting as [FACT] and the solid-vs-hollow dimension with its tradeoff
workflow.gate: all construction methods and the solid-vs-hollow dimension are stated with capital-heavy vs hand-ownable flags

workflow.description: List ear backs, jump rings, clasps, bails and pins as [FACT] bought-in components and the body+findings assembly model
workflow.gate: the findings taxonomy and the body+findings owner-scale assembly model are stated

workflow.description: Detail earrings, necklaces, rings, bracelets and anklets sub-types with per-type construction as [FACT]
workflow.gate: each category's sub-types and dominant construction are stated with the simplest sub-forms flagged

workflow.action: Assemble the category x construction matrix
workflow.description: Consolidate the five categories against construction, hollow/solid, plating mode and wear zone as the [FACT] reference artifact
workflow.gate: the full matrix is assembled as [FACT] with demand/price left as S1 pointers, not values

workflow.action: Map the plating/forming and geometry constraints
workflow.description: State the form-to-plating-mode/substrate/wear mapping and the Faraday-cage geometry-difficulty gradient
workflow.gate: the plating-mode mapping and the flat/convex-easy vs recessed/hollow/hinged-hard gradient are stated

workflow.action: Map wear zones and skin-contact/nickel by category
workflow.description: Rank abrasion exposure and skin-contact duration by category and tie to the EN1811/REACH nickel limits
workflow.gate: the wear-zone ranking and the pierced-ear/prolonged nickel limits are stated with S2 owning micron specs

workflow.action: Define the owner-scale envelope and complexity index
workflow.description: State the small-batch DIY-plating/no-foundry envelope and the weighted [METHOD] producibility score
workflow.gate: the envelope and the weighted index dimensions are stated as [METHOD]/[UNKNOWN], not a measured cost

workflow.description: Apply the index within the envelope to give the tiered simplest-to-hardest category ranking
workflow.gate: the three-tier ranking is stated as [METHOD/ESTIMATE] conditional on the envelope with the producibility-not-desirability caveat

workflow.action: Apply the modularity lever and the admission screen
workflow.description: State the standardize-invisible/vary-visible lever and the four-test admit/reject/redesign screen
workflow.gate: the modularity lever and the four all-must-pass screen tests are stated with reject-or-redesign outcomes

workflow.description: Separate [FACT] anchors from [METHOD/ESTIMATE] outputs and [UNKNOWN] inputs and route all demand questions to S1
workflow.gate: the FACT/METHOD/UNKNOWN partition is stated and every demand/price/share/demographic/brand question is assigned to S1

workflow.description: Deliver the tagged producible category set to kb2/kb3/S2/S5, stopping before style selection and demand ranking
workflow.gate: the tagged producible set is delivered to the four consumers with the clean pre-style/pre-demand boundary and honesty tags intact

priority_rationale: The three-axis frame, construction lexicon, findings taxonomy and plating/forming constraint map come first because every category description and producibility judgment reads off the same axes, methods, components and plating constraints; the five per-category sub-taxonomies and the consolidated matrix come next because they are the [FACT] reference the scoring operates on; the geometry-difficulty, wear-zone and skin-contact maps and the owner-scale envelope then supply the producibility inputs; the complexity index, simplest-to-produce ranking, modularity lever and admission screen apply those inputs to answer 'which is simplest to make at owner scale'; and the honesty ledger and hand-off come last because they bound the estimates, keep every demand question routed to S1, and package the producible category set for kb2/kb3/S2/S5.

dominance_rules.rule: The owner-scale envelope dominates any producibility claim
dominance_rules.rationale: a category is simple only relative to the small-batch DIY-plating/no-foundry envelope
dominance_rules.trigger: a producibility statement is made without its envelope condition
dominance_rules.action: attach the envelope condition and re-check the claim inside it, never quoting it at other scales

dominance_rules.rule: Plating-geometry difficulty dominates raw assembly count
dominance_rules.rationale: a low-part form that is Faraday-starved fails plating despite easy assembly
dominance_rules.trigger: a form is judged simple on component count alone
dominance_rules.action: score plating-geometry difficulty as its own dimension before calling the form simple

dominance_rules.rule: The nickel-safety benchmark dominates the cheapest-substrate choice for skin-contact forms
dominance_rules.rationale: pierced-ear and prolonged-contact forms carry a real allergy/regulatory limit
dominance_rules.trigger: a cheap high-nickel substrate is proposed for an earring post or prolonged-contact piece
dominance_rules.action: require a nickel-safe base or barrier plating regardless of the added cost

dominance_rules.rule: Wear zone dominates the hollow cost incentive
dominance_rules.rationale: hollow thin walls and starved interiors fail fastest exactly where abrasion is highest
dominance_rules.trigger: hollow construction is proposed for a medium/high-wear form to save metal
dominance_rules.action: keep solid construction in medium/high-wear zones; reserve hollow for low-wear categories

dominance_rules.rule: Fabricated ownable forms dominate cast forms in the current envelope
dominance_rules.rationale: there is no in-house foundry or automated setting line
dominance_rules.trigger: a cast or stone-set form is admitted without a capability check
dominance_rules.action: restrict to fabricated/formed forms or outsource/add capability before admitting the cast form

dominance_rules.rule: Producibility is necessary but does not dominate demand for the launch pick
dominance_rules.rationale: easy-to-make is not the same as sells-well, which is S1/S5's call
dominance_rules.trigger: a launch decision is made on producibility alone
dominance_rules.action: treat a screen pass as necessary-not-sufficient and defer the pick to S5 combining demand and style

dominance_rules.rule: The [FACT] taxonomy dominates the [METHOD] ranking on certainty
dominance_rules.rationale: the taxonomy is established fact while the ranking is a tunable envelope-conditional estimate
dominance_rules.trigger: the producibility ranking is stated as a fact
dominance_rules.action: label the ranking [METHOD/ESTIMATE] and keep the taxonomy as the firmer anchor

dominance_rules.rule: Static reliable closures dominate moving-part closures at owner scale
dominance_rules.rationale: hinges, lever-backs and tennis clasps are failure points that raise complexity
dominance_rules.trigger: a moving-part closure is chosen where a static one would serve
dominance_rules.action: default to endless hoops, friction backs and lobster clasps; add moving parts only when reliability is proven

dominance_rules.rule: The demand boundary dominates any market question asked of this KB
dominance_rules.rationale: the honesty contract forbids inventing demand/price/share/demographic/brand data
dominance_rules.trigger: a market question is posed to the form KB
dominance_rules.action: route it to S1 as [METHOD]/[UNKNOWN] and answer only the form part

anti_rework_rules.rule: Fix the three-axis frame and construction lexicon before enumerating categories
anti_rework_rules.prevents: category sub-taxonomies authored in inconsistent vocabulary that must later be re-normalized to one grid

anti_rework_rules.rule: Score plating-geometry difficulty alongside assembly count from the first pass
anti_rework_rules.prevents: ranking a form as simple on parts alone and discovering un-platable recesses after a build

anti_rework_rules.rule: Gate earring posts and prolonged-contact forms on the nickel benchmark before choosing a cheap substrate
anti_rework_rules.prevents: stamping a cheap high-nickel post line that must be recalled or re-substrated for skin safety

anti_rework_rules.rule: Condition the producibility ranking on the owner envelope explicitly when first stated
anti_rework_rules.prevents: the ranking being reused at other scales and producing an inverted, wrong launch shortlist

anti_rework_rules.rule: Standardize invisible functional findings and vary only the visible body
anti_rework_rules.prevents: either a monotonous same-looking range or a proliferation of plating runs and jigs that must be consolidated later

anti_rework_rules.rule: Check the owner envelope for casting/setting capability before admitting any cast or stone-set form
anti_rework_rules.prevents: designing a cast stone-set ring the owner cannot make and re-scoping the whole assortment

anti_rework_rules.rule: Design vent/drain paths into hollow forms before plating them
anti_rework_rules.prevents: trapped-solution staining that scraps a hollow batch and forces a redesign

anti_rework_rules.rule: Keep every demand/price/share question out of this KB and routed to S1 from the outset
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an invented market figure contaminating the form KB that must later be retracted for the honesty audit

iteration_protocol.trigger: the owner-scale equipment envelope changes (casting/setting added, larger plating bath, more rack capacity)
iteration_protocol.action: re-run the complexity index, the simplest-to-produce ranking and the screen inside the new envelope

iteration_protocol.trigger: real build outcomes let the complexity-index weights be calibrated
iteration_protocol.action: recalibrate the index weights and re-sort the ranking

iteration_protocol.trigger: a plating-geometry starvation or wear-through QC failure recurs on a form class
iteration_protocol.action: downgrade that geometry/wear class in the difficulty maps and the screen

iteration_protocol.trigger: S2 updates substrate, plating-thickness or nickel-safe-base guidance
iteration_protocol.action: update the plating-constraint and skin-contact maps and the screen's wear/nickel tests

iteration_protocol.trigger: a nickel-reaction or skin-contact return signal appears on posts/prolonged-contact forms
iteration_protocol.action: re-gate the affected forms on the nickel benchmark and update the skin-contact map

iteration_protocol.trigger: a new worn-location category or recurrent hybrid form enters scope
iteration_protocol.action: add its sub-taxonomy and matrix row and score it through the index and screen

iteration_protocol.trigger: S1 demand or kb2 style signals are ready to be combined downstream
iteration_protocol.action: confirm the hand-off tags and pass the producible set to S5 without conflating producibility with demand

required_checks: all edge ids unique EDGE_XXX format
all from/to in edges reference valid node ids
all competency_question_refs resolve to valid CQ ids
all evidence_refs resolve to valid source_registry ids
all priority_order entries are valid node ids with no duplicates
high_risk_nodes (risk_if_wrong>=0.80) have non-empty acceptance_tests and human_review_required=true
conflict edges have signed_tension<0 and resolution_rule present
observed_impact=0.0 for all nodes (no observed data)
19-24 nodes, 32-40 edges, 8-10 conflict_axes, 10-12 edge_cases, 9-12 workflow steps
post_formula_checks: all derived fields non-zero after compute run
